question: What is the primary purpose of negative feedback loops in endocrine regulation?

options.A: To maintain homeostasis and prevent excessive hormone levels
options.B: To amplify initial signals until an organ is exhausted
options.C: To permanently shut down endocrine gland function
options.D: To accelerate the metabolic breakdown of circulating proteins

explanation: Negative feedback counteracts deviations from a set point, ensuring hormone concentrations remain within safe, functional physiological ranges. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T6#GNS211_U1_T6_h4)

question: What defines contrast-induced nephropathy when monitoring a patient a few days after an IVP?

options.A: An acute, sudden rise in serum creatinine levels
options.B: The development of severe protein-losing enteropathy
options.C: An irreversible drop in systemic blood pressure
options.D: A permanent cessation of total urine production

question: What immediate action should a nurse take if a patient expels a suppository two minutes after insertion?

question: Why must a simple pneumothorax be actively managed before transporting a trauma patient?

options.A: Vibration from the vehicle will cause immediate rib fractures

options.C: Oxygen cylinders leak rapidly when exposed to low ground temperatures
options.D: The chest tube is required to anchor the patient to the stretcher

explanation: Altitude shifts or uneven road vibrations can worsen chest injuries, turning a manageable pneumothorax into a catastrophic tension state. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)?

options.A: To outline clear, time-bound milestones and support to correct skill deficits

options.C: To calculate the annual bonus allocation for senior hospital executives
